neighbours.label: the canonical character or object in a retelling of a famous story (Cheshire Cat, Macbeth's witches, Hamlet's father's ghost)
fire: In the Odyssey, the hero blinds the Cyclops and escapes from his cave.
Cinderella lost her glass slipper as the clock struck midnight.
Jack climbed the beanstalk and found a giant living above the clouds.
In Moby-Dick, Captain Ahab hunts the white whale across the oceans.
Little Red Riding Hood met a wolf on her way to her grandmother's house.
Romeo drinks the poison in the tomb, believing Juliet is dead.
Pinocchio's nose grew longer every time he told a lie.
In the legend, King Arthur pulled the sword from the stone.
quiet: On the cruise, the tourist lost his camera and missed the ship's departure.
My cousin lost her left shoe as the party ended around midnight.
The boy climbed the ladder and found a bird's nest in the gutter.
On the trawler, the captain hunts tuna across the warm southern waters.
The little girl met a neighbor on her way to her grandmother's house.
The patient drinks the medicine at night, believing it will help him sleep.
My brother's face turned red every time he told a lie.
In the workshop, the old blacksmith pulled the sword from the fire.

notes: Card top: Narcissus' reflection, Macbeth's witches, Cheshire Cat, Othello's handkerchief (plus third-party / Underwriters Laboratories). Probe: Cheshire 0.71 and Hamlet's 'father' 0.70; a mirror in an ordinary sentence 0.20. The shared pattern looks like the expected element of a well-known story or fixed reference.
